recentItems.title: Victor Lewis-Smith on The James Whale Radio Show (1990)
recentItems.description:
Victor Lewis-Smith was no stranger to appearing on television shows - even if he himself said that his wrinkled visage would be far too grotesque to be contained inside the magic rectangle (in fact, he was once told "I've seen better hair on a coconut").

One such show was The James Whale Radio Show, which featured lavatories as one episode's theme. Naturally, Victor jumped at the chance to appear on the show - live from his luxury York penthouse flat - and showcase his new song "Sitting On My Bog".

"Sitting On My Bog", incidentally, was never released as an actual song - because nobody in their right mind thought that anyone in their right mind would buy it.

recentItems.title: Victor Lewis-Smith's Look at Life - Cockermouth TV (1991)
recentItems.description:
With the ITV Franchise Auctions coming up, Victor seizes another opportunity to get onto the telly. Rounding up a crack team consisting of Michael Grade, Alan Yentob, Bill Cotton, David Frost and Myra Hindley, he creates his own franchise called "Cockermouth TV".

Originally broadcast as part of BBC Radio 4's "Loose Ends" programme, "Victor Lewis-Smith's Look at Life" was where most people of a certain generation first heard Victor's voice. 

These were short radio pieces that stuck out from the usual round table discussions on "Loose Ends", consisting of breakneck speed tape-wind-festooned listener-scaring reports on whatever took Victor's fancy.
